english.notes:
(i) A brothel is a place resorted to by persons of opposite sexes for the purpose of illicit intercourse, although it is not necessary that the women using the premises are prostitutes or that payments are made to them; Winter v Woolfe [1931] 1 KB 549.
(ii) The use of premises as a brothel is a matter of fact for the jury to decide, the whole or part of a house may be used where there is use by more than one prostitute.
(iii) Premises which are resorted to for the purposes of lewd homosexual practices shall be treated as brothels for the purposes of sections 33, 34, and 35 of this Act and section 6 of the Sexual Offences Act 1967.
(iv) The wording of the offence implies a permission by the tenant or occupier given to some other woman or women, therefore a woman who is a sole occupier, using the premises for her own habitual prostitution, cannot be convicted of 'permitting' the premises to be used; Singleton v Ellison [1895] 1 QB 607.
(v) On second or subsequent conviction - Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.
(vi) MoPI notes: this offence may be MoPI Group 3 if there is no gain/control/exploitation/coercion suspected. Manual review recommended.
